# Public capability support matrix

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/rebuild/gen_support_matrix.py. Do not edit by
     hand; re-run the generator. `--check` fails if this file drifts. -->

One row per PUBLIC CAPABILITY, with the evidence that exists for it as of
the revisions in `RELEASE_REVISIONS.txt`. A capability is not listed because it
is exported; it is listed because the packet asked a question about it and
something measured the answer.

**`documentation` is not evidence of behaviour.** A row whose `evidence_class` is
`documentation` has prose behind it and nothing else; it is listed so that it is
not silently absent, and it is excluded from the passing-evidence count.

**A certificate is not a measurement.** ADR-003 separates a *numeric* verification
(a measurement that passed against a stated tolerance) from a *strict certificate*
(an original-coordinate certificate that is constructed and checked). A row whose
`evidence_class` is `certificate` claims the second; a row whose class is
`numeric_verified` claims only the first, and reading it as a certificate is the
confusion ADR-003 exists to prevent. No row in this table is `certificate`.

A capability counts under **with passing evidence** when its `evidence_class`
is not `documentation` and it has at least one passing acceptance item or a
passing `Test Summary` corroboration. Prose-only rows are listed so that they
are not silently absent, and are never counted.

**`certified` is 0.** Every row here is `numeric_or_structural_verified`,
`partial`, `certificate_gap` or `prose_only`. A numerically verified
capability has a measurement that passed against a stated tolerance; a
*strictly certified* one additionally has an original-coordinate certificate
(ADR-003). The two are different states, and this table is where a reader can
see which one they are looking at. Nothing in this release is certified.

## Every row that is not `verified`

Listed in full, because the failure this table exists to prevent is a
reader assuming the unlisted rows are fine.

### `SDPX-COMPILE` — Compile a user problem into a canonical form with a reversible transform stack — `partially_verified`

* level: `partial`   evidence class: `numeric_verified`
* passing acceptance items: 10 of 14; passing log corroborations: 5
* non-passing evidence rows:
  * `S01[0].acceptance` = `partially_verified` — Round-trip maps, equality elimination and the objective offset pass an independent fixture
    * evidence: test/rebuild/S01.jl testsets 'S01 rsoc transform vs A01 oracle' (44), 'S01 nonpositive transform' (12), 'S01 equality elimination' (43), 'S01 objective offset replay' (11); all pass in both environments (rebuild-reports/S01/logs/S01_default_env.log, S01_rebuild_env.log). Round trips use A01's reference_oracles.jl (zero SDPX calls) for the RSOC convention and Rational{BigInt} for exact comparisons. LIMIT: A01's fixtures.jl is used as the MODEL description (block order and cone kinds), not as an oracle that hands over expected canonical arrays - the expected values are recomputed in-test from the model's own statements and from c_D' * x_particular. Also, the equality-elimination fixture is a purpose-built program, not one of A01's named fixtures.
  * `S01[1].acceptance` = `partially_verified` — Mutating the original user input must not affect an already-admitted problem
    * evidence: testset 'S01 compiled problem ownership' (30 pass): after in-place mutation of objective_vector, rhs and equality_matrix.nzval, admits_original_input(compiled) becomes false while canonical objective, A and b are byte-identical to their pre-mutation copies, the snapshot storage is distinct from the program arrays, and a separately built reduction is unaffected. LIMIT: the mutated object is the NativeConeProgram produced by compile_product_cone_model, not a user-facing Model or an MOI optimizer instance. I did NOT execute a mutation through the MOI layer or through the frontend Model after admission, so 'the raw user Model is isolated' is demonstrated at the level of the compiled input snapshot, which is the artefact ADR-001 s2 assigns to this layer.
  * `S01[3].acceptance` = `partially_verified` — The public/MOI layer no longer applies separate sign patches
    * evidence: src/core/compiled_problem.jl records every canonical sign decision as OWNED (CanonicalBlockMap.sign, located per row by canonical_transform_map) and StackedSignTransform expresses the sign as a whole-vector entry wherever that is well-defined; replay_public_signs reports owned_signs == number of canonical blocks, unowned_signs == 0, public_sign_patches == 0 (asserted in testset 'S01 compiled problem ownership'). A static repo-wide grep of src/public/, src/moi_wrapper.jl and src/frontend/ found no separate sign patch. LIMIT: this is an ownership-plus-static-grep claim. I did NOT run an MOI solve before and after to show a runtime sign patch disappearing, because removing an existing public-layer patch is an edit to an existing source file, which is I01 authority and outside this card's allowlist. The deliverable is the mechanism plus the audit hook; the deletion of any public-layer patch belongs to I01.
  * `S01[2].log` = `not_run` — log verdict for commands[2]
    * evidence: rebuild-reports/S01/logs/pkgtest.log
  * `S01.numeric_test` = `unsupported` — MultiFloat leg
    * evidence: Runs and passes (8 assertions) under --project=$REBUILD_ENV with the SDPXMultiFloatLinearAlgebraExt extension loaded. In the DEFAULT project it is unsupported and reported as Broken with the reason 'MultiFloatLinearAlgebra is not resolvable in .../Project.toml; run with --project=$REBUILD_ENV' - never a silent pass.
  * `S01.numeric_test` = `unsupported` — QDLRL
    * evidence: Base.find_package("QDLRL") is nothing in the default project and in REBUILD_ENV. Not needed by S01; recorded as a missing dependency (infrastructure), not a numeric failure.
  * `S02[2].acceptance` = `partially_verified` — 没有第二个被生产调用的HSD loop (no second HSD loop called by production)
    * evidence: S02-D (8 assertions): STATIC source scan shows exactly one iterate-advancing loop in the extraction (solver_run_session!), one epoch-executor call site, and that src/SDPX.jl does not include src/solver/loop.jl, so production today calls only product_hsd_solve!. NOT dynamically proven: this is a textual static argument, explicitly labelled STATIC, and it is not a runtime call-graph proof.
  * `S02[3].log` = `not_run` — log verdict for commands[3]
    * evidence: rebuild-reports/S02/pkgtest_run.log

### `PROVIDER-CONCURRENT-PRECISION` — Concurrent sessions at different precisions, in-process and in parallel — `not_verified`

* level: `partial`   evidence class: `contract`
* passing acceptance items: 1 of 2; passing log corroborations: 8
* blocked by: This is the ONE REQUIRED ROW that P03's release gate reports FAIL (`release_gate_verdict = FAIL`, `release_gate_failing_rows = ["concurrent_sessions_different_precision_in_process_parallel"]`, `required = true`, state `unsupported`). PARENT_FINDINGS_BATCH5.md F10 records that the parent confirmed `required = true` at the source and DECLINED to demote it so the gate would pass. No passing artifact exists.
* non-passing evidence rows:
  * `P03[0].acceptance` = `partially_verified` — Concurrent sessions at DIFFERENT PRECISIONS actually verified; if this cannot be resolved, keep it as an explicit prototype / unsupported and do not label it production-ready
    * evidence: Verified cross-process (two -t1 children at 256/512, launched before either was waited on, both correct against their own precision's oracle, distinct digests and unit roundoffs) and verified in-process in a serialized interleaved mode (two @async tasks, ambient restored on every call, precision observed inside each call was the session's own). NOT verified in-process in parallel: unsupported with a measured reason (process-global BigFloat precision plus the provider's own _ambient_guard requiring ambient == cache bits and nthreads == 1). The adapter is NOT labelled production-ready: the release gate is FAIL on exactly that row. See rebuild-reports/P03/P03_run_main.txt lines ambient_second_precision_refused, serialized_precision_*_ambient_observed_inside, child_*_stdout.
  * `P03[7].log` = `fail` — log verdict for commands[7]
    * evidence: rebuild-reports/P03/P03_verdict_pin_control_old.log
  * `P03.numeric_test` = `unsupported` — concurrent sessions at DIFFERENT PRECISIONS, in-process, :ambient policy
    * evidence: Reason, measured: BigFloat precision is process-global and BFLASparseLDLCache calls _ambient_guard, which throws PrecisionMismatch unless precision(BigFloat) == cache.precision_bits and ArgumentError unless Threads.nthreads() == 1. Constructing a 512-bit session at ambient 256 throws PrecisionMismatch; using a live 256-bit session after the ambient moved to 512 throws AmbientState. Two sessions at different precisions cannot both be live in one process. Recorded unsupported, NOT counted as a pass, and this is the row that fails the release gate.
  * `P03.numeric_test` = `unsupported` — provider in-place numeric refactorization capability
    * evidence: Reason, measured: isdefined(BigFloatLinearAlgebra, :refactorize!) == false at this revision - the name does not exist, so there is no in-place numeric refactor entry point to exercise. This confirms ADR-004 section 4's declared asymmetry (numeric_refactor_in_place = false) at the code level. No fallback was invented and no route was silently used instead.
  * `P03.numeric_test` = `not_run` — native (MPFR limb / malloc) allocator accounting
    * evidence: Reason: no MPFR limb counter and no malloc interposer is available in this process, so this measurement was NOT RUN and no number is reported for it - not 0. RSS is the only native-level signal taken, and it is reported with its unit calibrated above. Julia-heap allocation and BigFloat cell identity are measured separately (previous entry).
  * `P03.numeric_test` = `fail` — release gate computation
    * evidence: GATE VERDICT: FAIL, and this entry's status is deliberately fail so that nothing in this report can be read as a passing release. 14 capability rows are computed from the measured booleans of the same run: 10 are required and 9 of those are verified, so the verdict is FAIL. The verdict is MEASURED AND LOGGED, NOT ASSERTED: an earlier version of the driver wrote '@test gate_failure == true', which pinned the red outcome and made the driver fail on a revision where the capability is implemented - the mirror image of counting a skip as a pass. What is asserted now is the RULE (three synthetic controls: required+unsupported must fail, required+verified must pass, optional+unsupported must pass) plus an independent re-derivation of the verdict from the rows (10 required vs 9 verified-required). Exactly one REQUIRED row is unsupported: concurrent_sessions_different_precision_in_process_parallel. The high-precision sparse capability itself is verified at 256/512/1024, so the gate does not fail on that ground.
